name: human-search-profile
purpose: Defines how agents should search more like a careful human researcher: expand queries, use operators, diversify source lanes, snowball from strong seeds, summarize useful findings, and record why weak sources were ignored.

reader_guide.summary: Use this profile when web search quality matters, especially before research, planning, governance, source collection, coding research, deep research, marketing evidence research, or reusable knowledge capture.
how_to_read: Start with trigger_situations to decide whether this profile is needed.
Use human_search_stages as the execution order.
Use query_ladder_templates to generate multiple searches instead of repeating one keyword.
Use source_lane_targets to avoid over-relying on one source family.
Use snowballing_rules after the first strong seeds are found.
Use summary_capture_contract when deciding which good sources deserve a reusable summary.
update_triggers: Search results repeatedly miss important source families.
A new search provider, API, browser automation flow, or source collector adapter is added.
Agents cite search results without opening pages or without recording why sources matter.
Deep research, source discovery, or web-first intake workflows change.

structure_rules.rule: Do not treat the first result page as the research. Run at least one query expansion pass and one source-lane pass for research or governance work.
structure_rules.reason: Important sources often appear through alternate wording, exact phrases, operators, source-family searches, or cited references.

structure_rules.rule: Use operators only with a reason: exact match for named concepts, site search for source families, filetype search for PDFs/reports, date terms for freshness, and exclusion for spam or sponsored results.
structure_rules.reason: Operators improve precision only when tied to an explicit evidence gap.

structure_rules.rule: Snowballing should start from strong seed sources, then follow references, cited-by links, authors, repositories, talks, datasets, or related sources.
structure_rules.reason: Weak seed sources lead to noisy snowballing and shallow summaries.

structure_rules.rule: Summarize sources only when they change the answer, plan, risk model, reusable knowledge base, or future source list.
structure_rules.reason: The goal is better future work, not a large pile of low-value notes.

structure_rules.rule: Likes, votes, stars, comments, Reddit/HN/LinkedIn activity, and search ranking are discovery or adoption signals, not standalone factual proof.
structure_rules.reason: Popularity can reveal practical interest but does not guarantee accuracy.

field_guide.meaning: When to apply this profile instead of a minimal web-first search.
Execution stages from scope and query ladder through snowballing, triage, summary capture, and search record.
Reusable query transformations for seed, synonym, operator, source-family, regional, community, and contrary searches.
Source families that should be represented before treating broad research as complete.
When and how to summarize high-value sources for future reuse.

trigger_situations: The user asks for better web search, deeper source discovery, or many sources.
A plan, architecture, research note, or recommendation depends on external references.
The task may benefit from official sources, papers, implementation examples, expert analysis, community signals, and contrary cases.
The output should create reusable research notes or update a source registry.

examples: {topic} best practices OR checklist OR playbook
{topic} implementation OR architecture OR case study
{topic} arxiv OR ACM OR IEEE OR paper

operator_patterns.use_when: The topic is a named concept, product, method, error, report title, or quote.
A specific source family matters, such as official docs, GitHub, Stack Overflow, Reddit, Korean tech blogs, or a publisher site.
Reports, papers, manuals, slide decks, standards, or methodology PDFs are likely.
Search results are polluted by sponsored, low-quality, duplicated, or unrelated pages.
The fact may have changed recently; include current year, release, changelog, last updated, or date-restricted searches.

snowballing_rules: Choose 3 to 5 strong seed sources after source triage.
Run backward snowballing through references, bibliographies, linked reports, linked repositories, and cited tools.
Run forward snowballing through cited-by pages, later articles, related papers, GitHub dependents, issues, and conference talks.
Record followed links, rejected links, why each mattered, and whether it changed the plan.
Stop when new snowball passes no longer produce higher-quality sources or contradictions.
source_triage_rules: Open the source before relying on it; search result titles are not evidence.
Record source type, publisher, author when available, date, source value, key claim, reliability, limitation, and plan impact.
Rank official, primary, paper, standard, maintained code, and methodology-transparent sources above commentary for factual claims.
Use commentary, social, and community sources to find practical problems, adoption signals, and contradictions.
Downgrade sources with missing dates, unclear authorship, obvious marketing incentives, no methodology, or unsupported numbers.
summary_capture_contract: Create or update a reusable _research note when a source bundle will likely help future work.
Summaries should be short, source-grounded, and linked to exact URLs or repository paths.
Each summary should state applicability, reliability, uncertainty, and what future tasks should verify again.
Do not archive long copyrighted passages; summarize and quote only short compliant excerpts when necessary.
